test_title: PYST 50: SSC GD Constable 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 07 Mar, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: Rupesh scored 20 percent marks in an exam and failed by 20 marks. If he scores 70 percent marks, then he gets 5 marks more than passing marks. What should be the passing marks for the exam?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in percentage = 70% − 20% = 50%

Difference in marks = 20 (failed by) + 5 (excess) = 25 marks

∴ 50% of total marks = 25 marks

→ 10% of total marks = 5 marks

Passing marks = (20% of total) + 20 = (2 × 5) + 20 = 30 marks

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1 score = 20% of Total, Deficit from passing = 20 marks

Case 2 score = 70% of Total, Excess over passing = 5 marks

**Formula Used:**

Passing marks = (Score percentage × Total Marks) + Deficit = (Score percentage × Total Marks) − Excess

 
• 20% Marks Fail by 20 Passing Point 70% Marks Extra 5 
 Gap = 50% = 25 Marks 

⇒ Let the total marks be x.

⇒ (20/100) × x + 20 = (70/100) × x − 5

⇒ 0.20x + 20 = 0.70x − 5

⇒ 0.70x − 0.20x = 20 + 5

⇒ 0.50x = 25

⇒ x = 25 ÷ 0.50 = 50

⇒ Passing marks = 20% of 50 + 20

⇒ Passing marks = (20/100) × 50 + 20

⇒ Passing marks = 10 + 20 = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Marks Formula

Total Marks = (Difference in marks obtained ÷ Difference in percentage) × 100.

Passing Percentage

Passing Percentage = (Passing Marks ÷ Total Marks) × 100. It is the minimum percent required to pass the exam.

Percentage Change

Percentage change = (Difference ÷ Original Value) × 100. This is used to find growth or reduction in scores.
